newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Norilsk union still seeks pay rise.
newsitem.headline: Russian Norilsk union still seeks pay rise.

text.p: Workers at Russia's Norilsk Nickel metals combine are not satisfied with the results of talks with management on salary arrears and rises, a senior trade union official said on Friday.

"We have not reached normal relations with the management," said Valery Glazkov, chairman of the combine's United Trade Union Committee, which he said represented 100,000 union members and which is the main trade union organisation. But he said there were no disruptions to output or to loadings for export.
"We are still standing by our demand for a pay raise," he said by telephone from the Arctic town of Norilsk where the flagship plant is based.
Employee representatives would meet management on March 1 for talks, he said, adding he expected the talks to be "lively".
Salary arrears total 1.3 trillion roubles and workers are demanding that wages be boosted by what a RAO Norilsky Nickel spokesman said earlier would cost the company 70 billion roubles a month.
Russian news agencies have said that a reconciliation commission grouping management and labour had agreed an arrears repayment schedule through 1997.
The Norilsk group is a major producer of nickel, copper, platinum, palladium and other metals.
